findings.title: The finder wall strips the evidence bundles.json cites, so D15's universe enumerator refuses in every finder tree
findings.claim: After tools/audit/prepare_baseline.sh --strip <tree> 11, `tools/audit/enumerate.py d15-installs` refuses (exit 2) on a tree where it printed 1 line before the strip, because strip_earlier_rounds keeps only round files cited by tests/closures.json or tests/*.py|mjs|sh and bundles.json's evidence path is neither.
findings.mechanism: strip_earlier_rounds' keep set (closures + literal paths in tests/*) and enumerate.py:d15's existence requirement on bundles.json[].evidence are two definitions of which earlier-round files a finder tree must hold; the D15 brief names `enumerate.py d15-installs` as the universe, so the seat whose dimension it is cannot enumerate it in its own tree (observed in this seat's export: REFUSE ... round10/D15/s1/intake.py is not in the tree). Of the 19 universes enumerate.py serves, only d15-installs refuses in the walled export.

evidence.machine: macOS arm64, box B8 (shared), CI venv python3
evidence.contention_note: shared box, other finder seats running; counts are contention-immune

perturbation.change: --cite-in-tests: plant one tests/*.py citing the evidence path (the strip's own keep rule)

null_control.note: the evidence's own round is not stripped, so the enumerator answers

findings.metric_definition: Lines enumerate.py d15-installs prints in a planted tree after prepare_baseline.sh --strip; -1 when it refuses.
findings.phenomenon_property: Every path an enumerate.py universe requires to exist survives the finder wall that prepares the tree the universe's dimension runs in.
findings.seam_rule: for each universe U in enumerate.py's docstring: bash tools/audit/prepare_baseline.sh --strip <copy> <round> && python3 tools/audit/enumerate.py U --repo <copy> (exit 2 = a seam); at the baseline only d15-installs
findings.proposed_fix_scope: Keep dev/audit/config/*.json-cited evidence paths in strip_earlier_rounds' keep set (one more glob beside tests/*), or have enumerate.py d15 read the evidence from git when the tree is walled; either way a self-test arm in prepare_baseline.sh --strip-self-test planting a bundles.json citation.
reproduction_steps: python3 tools/audit/enumerate.py d15-installs (in the finder export): REFUSE

findings.title: D15.md step 2's privacy gate over the bundle refuses its own null-control bundle, so every D15 run stops at M2
findings.claim: export.violations over the debug bundle, the scope D15.md M2 names, returns 72 violations on the synthetic dbg_bundle_gen.py bundle (no private datum by construction) and 1102 on the owner's real download with 0 true private hits, while over the sealed replay half (the scope tools/replay/debug_ingest.py stage 2 gates) both return 0.
findings.mechanism: replay_doc.text_ok is the allowlist for a committed public replay fixture; the debug bundle's other sections carry text the integration itself writes (release strings in every cycle row, Home Assistant's redaction marker, insight and ledger prose that the ADDRESS regex reads as 'a word, then a house number', month keys). D15.md M2 and debug_ingest.py hold two definitions of the gate's scope; under the brief's, 'either failing stops the run' fires on every bundle including the null control (round 10 left M2 unfinished on it, item C1). The marker refusal is a second seam: _no_credential does not accept '**REDACTED**', so each redacted credential key reads as 'a credential-named key carries a value' (61 marker leaves refused in the real download).

evidence.value: synthetic_violations=72 (scope whole), real_violations=1102, real_private_hits=0, replay-half 0/0, leak_probe_controls_green=46/46, planted arms caught 5/5 per bundle

findings.title: store.DOMAINS declares less than the writers write; the debug ring's loader drops rows with an unpriced sample
findings.claim: A sample the coordinator writes with predicted_cost None (no price covered the interval, #2229) is outside DOMAINS (admitted=0), so debugger._kept refuses each debugger.cycle_row row that carries it: 0 of 192 rows kept for the synthetic bundle's production-written samples; and on the owner's real download 102 healthy fields its loaders read intact are off their declaration (off_restore 1, snapshots 101).
findings.mechanism: DOMAINS['accuracy']['accuracy/samples/#/predicted_cost'] is _R (non-null) while AccuracySample.as_dict writes None and actual_cost beside it is _N; 'rows/#/accuracy_sample' aliases that table and debugger._repair drops a row admitted() refuses, so the ring loses those rows on the next load (restart). The same drift without a dropping reader: off_restore 'armed/*' is declared a number while its writer stores {entity_id, value} and _entry_of reads that mapping; the snapshot ring keeps the pre-R10-HOTFIX-COP-UNMEASURED learner keys cop_baseline/cop_health_cusum, which DOMAINS neither declares nor marks unread. The stores self-test (debugger.store_report) reports these as off-domain on a healthy install.

evidence.value: sample_none_cost_admitted=0, unit_row_kept=0/1, synthetic_written_rows_kept=0/192 (192/192 unpriced), real off_domain[off_restore]=1 with loader keeping 2/2, real off_domain[snapshots]=101

findings.title: A capacity-envelope bucket the fold writes with count 0 is dropped by its own loader at every restart
findings.claim: _fold_capacity_envelope seeds a bucket as [heat_kw, 0] for a measured heat sample at partial load, _thermal_learning_payload stores it, and _load_t4b_learners refuses it through _learned_pair (count < 1): 1 bucket written, 0 reloaded; the owner's live thermal-learning store holds 1 such bucket and the loader restores 0 of it.
findings.mechanism: One fact decided twice: the fold (#1955 fold e) treats a measured delivered-heat sample as a floor that 'never counts towards capping' and so keeps count 0, while the loader's _learned_pair (and DOMAINS 'capacity_envelope/*/1': int >= 1) holds that a fold writes an entry only at its first counted sample. The floor learned between restarts is discarded at each load (and at a snapshot restore, which shares the parser); the next nameplate sample then starts from max(thermal_kw, nothing) instead of the remembered floor.

evidence.value: fold_written=1, fold_written_count_zero=1, reloaded=0, lost=1; bundle_stored=1, bundle_zero_count=1, bundle_reloaded=0; bundle_snapshot_zero_count_buckets=2
evidence.machine: macOS arm64, box B8 (shared), CI venv python3

perturbation.change: --loader-accepts-zero: coordinator._learned_pair accepts a count of 0 (the one-line loader edit)

null_control.note: a sample at nameplate counts, so the loader keeps the bucket: the loss is confined to the partial-load floor

findings.metric_definition: Buckets of _capacity_envelope the fold wrote minus those a fresh coordinator holds after _load_t4b_learners reads _thermal_learning_payload's JSON.
findings.phenomenon_property: Every [value, count] pair a fold writes is restored by its loader: a fold's stored count domain equals its loader's.
findings.seam_rule: grep -nE "setdefault\([^)]*\[[^]]*, *0\]\)" custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/*.py, each seeded pair against the loader its store key reaches (baseline: coordinator.py capacity_envelope, a seam; freq_control.py buckets, increments before any save and its loader accepts count >= 0, not a seam)
findings.proposed_fix_scope: Decide the count's meaning once: either the loader (a capacity-envelope-specific parse) and DOMAINS accept count 0 for the measured floor, or the fold stores the floor apart from the counted envelope; a round-trip regression arm through _thermal_learning_payload and _load_t4b_learners.
